primary_problem_source.title: Mathematical exploration and discovery at scale
primary_problem_source.location: Section 6.47, printed page 57 in the supplied text extraction.
primary_problem_source.quoted_scope_summary: Problem 6.47 defines Duchi's variant with the unitarily invariant norm inside each summand. It states m>=4 is open, lists (4,4,3) among AlphaEvolve's parameter choices, includes Schatten 2 among tested norms, and reports no construction improving the identity upper bound 1.

traditional_source.title: Commentary on 'Towards a Noncommutative Arithmetic-Geometric Mean Inequality'
traditional_source.author: John C. Duchi
traditional_source.venue: COLT 2012, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research volume 23, pages 11.25-11.27
traditional_source.role: Defines the with- and without-replacement expectations and introduces the product-norm-inside-sum variant. The identity tuple is the standard exact witness for the value 1.

reference_witness.result: All 256 and 24 product norms equal sqrt(3), so the ratio is exactly 1.

related_but_distinct_results.title: Recht-Re Noncommutative Arithmetic-Geometric Mean Conjecture is False
related_but_distinct_results.distinction: This refutes the Recht-Re formulation with a norm outside the sum; it does not refute the Duchi inside-sum ratio.

related_but_distinct_results.title: Exact Low-Length Recht-Re Inequalities and Metric-Dependent Rankings in Random Reshuffling Dynamics
related_but_distinct_results.status: Unrefereed candidate release; it concerns Recht-Re's outside-sum comparison and states that no unaffiliated rerun is recorded. It does not address the Duchi norm-inside-sum target.

rational_domain_density: For any Hermitian PSD A, A+epsilon*I is positive definite. Complex rational Hermitian matrices are dense among Hermitian matrices, so sufficiently close rational Hermitian approximants to A+epsilon*I stay positive definite. Letting epsilon tend to zero approximates A. The objective is continuous wherever its without-replacement denominator is positive; close approximants preserve positivity. Therefore restricting to exact rational entries leaves the infimum unchanged.
